translation: Machine translation (Claude, 5 Nov 2026) of the reviewed Indonesian file next to it; needs owner review. Same ids, option order and correct answers as the Indonesian source (decision 0185).
schemaNote: decision 0017: per-object questions; mc follows decision 0013 (correct + wrong[3]); every quote is verbatim in its sourceChunk text or in one of its PDF-verified table rows (assets/module/module_chunks.json)

items.question: Which waste group does a broken mobile phone belong to in three-group sorting?
items.correct: B3, because besides metal it also contains hazardous materials
wrong: Organic, because microorganisms can break it down
Ordinary non-organic, because it only contains metal and plastic
Residual waste that goes straight to the landfill
items.explanation: A phone is e-waste: it has metals but also hazardous materials, so the module treats it as B3 waste.
items.quote: Perangkat elektronik rusak (e-waste) mengandung logam, tetapi juga mengandung bahan berbahaya sehingga dibahas sebagai sampah B3 di Bab 2.

items.question: Before an old phone is handed in at an e-waste collection point, what should its owner do?
items.correct: Delete personal data first
wrong: Take the battery out themselves
Burn the plastic case
Soak the circuit board in acid
items.explanation: The module asks for e-waste to be handed in at a collection point after personal data is deleted; taking it apart, burning it or soaking it in acid is forbidden or dangerous.
items.quote: Serahkan ke titik pengumpulan e-waste; hapus data pribadi lebih dulu

items.question: Why is the lithium battery inside a broken phone dangerous?
items.correct: It can catch fire if damaged or crushed (thermal runaway)
wrong: It is safe to burn with ordinary waste
Microorganisms can break it down into compost
It is safe to take apart yourself for its metals
items.explanation: The module says Li-ion phone batteries can catch fire if damaged or crushed and often start fires in garbage trucks and landfills.
items.quote: Baterai rusak atau tertekan dapat terbakar (thermal runaway); sering memicu kebakaran di truk sampah dan TPA.

items.question: Which metals can be recovered from an old phone, and who may recover them?
items.correct: Copper, aluminium, gold and silver, by licensed facilities
wrong: Copper and gold, by the phone owner burning the cables
Mercury, by a waste bank heating the circuit board
No metals can be recovered, so phones are buried in the landfill
items.explanation: For e-waste such as phones, licensed facilities can recover copper, aluminium, gold, silver and other metals; people only need to sort and hand it in.
items.quote: Tembaga, aluminium, emas, perak dan logam lain

items.question: Explain how a broken phone should be handled from home until it is handed in, and why it must not go in an ordinary bin.

rubricPoints.point: A phone is e-waste that contains hazardous materials, so it is B3.
rubricPoints.quote: Perangkat elektronik rusak (e-waste) mengandung logam, tetapi juga mengandung bahan berbahaya sehingga dibahas sebagai sampah B3 di Bab 2.

rubricPoints.point: Hand it in at an e-waste collection point and delete personal data first.
rubricPoints.quote: Serahkan ke titik pengumpulan e-waste; hapus data pribadi lebih dulu

rubricPoints.point: Its lithium battery can catch fire if damaged or crushed.
rubricPoints.quote: Baterai rusak atau tertekan dapat terbakar (thermal runaway); sering memicu kebakaran di truk sampah dan TPA.

rubricPoints.point: If thrown away with ordinary waste, landfill leachate carries heavy metals into the soil and groundwater.
rubricPoints.quote: B3 yang terbuang bersama sampah biasa menumpuk di TPA, lalu lindi (cairan rembesan) membawa logam berat ke tanah dan air tanah.

items.question: Where should a broken laptop be handed in?
items.correct: At an e-waste collection point
wrong: In the organic waste bin
In the ordinary inorganic waste bin
At a waste fire in the yard
items.explanation: The module lists laptops as e-waste to be handed in at an e-waste collection point after personal data is deleted.
items.quote: Serahkan ke titik pengumpulan e-waste; hapus data pribadi lebih dulu

items.question: Why must an old laptop not be burned together with other waste?
items.correct: Burning waste mixed with B3 releases toxic smoke, heavy metals and dioxins
wrong: A laptop is organic waste that must be composted
Burning turns the laptop's metals into methane
A laptop may be burned as long as its battery is taken out first
items.explanation: The module explains that open burning of waste mixed with B3 releases toxic smoke, heavy metals and dioxins; taking batteries out yourself is also forbidden.
items.quote: Pembakaran terbuka sampah bercampur B3 melepas asap beracun, logam berat, dan dioksin ke udara.

items.question: Which substances inside broken electronics such as a laptop make them toxic?
items.correct: Lead, mercury, cadmium and the batteries inside
wrong: Cellulose fibres and lignin
Food scraps and oil
Methane and carbon dioxide
items.explanation: The module lists lead, mercury, cadmium, flame retardants and batteries as hazardous substances in broken electronics.
items.quote: Timbal, merkuri, kadmium, bahan penghambat api, baterai di dalamnya.

items.question: A technician burns old laptop cables and soaks its circuit board in acid to get the metals out. Why is this dangerous?
items.correct: It is very dangerous for workers and the environment; B3 recycling may only be done by licensed facilities
wrong: It is recommended because it counts as recycle in the 3R principle
It is safe as long as it is done outdoors
It is fine because metals from laptops are not dangerous
items.explanation: The module warns that informal e-waste recycling is very dangerous and that B3 recycling may only be done by licensed facilities.
items.quote: Daur ulang e-waste secara informal (membakar kabel, merendam papan sirkuit dengan asam) sangat berbahaya bagi pekerja dan lingkungan.

items.question: Explain why a broken laptop is B3 waste and what its owner's role is in managing it.

rubricPoints.point: A laptop is e-waste that contains hazardous materials, so it is B3.
rubricPoints.quote: Perangkat elektronik rusak (e-waste) mengandung logam, tetapi juga mengandung bahan berbahaya sehingga dibahas sebagai sampah B3 di Bab 2.

rubricPoints.point: The owner's role is to sort it, store it safely and hand it in.
rubricPoints.quote: Peran masyarakat adalah memilah, menyimpan aman, dan menyetor.

rubricPoints.point: It is handed in at an e-waste collection point after personal data is deleted.
rubricPoints.quote: Serahkan ke titik pengumpulan e-waste; hapus data pribadi lebih dulu

rubricPoints.point: Informal recycling (burning cables, soaking circuit boards in acid) is very dangerous.
rubricPoints.quote: Daur ulang e-waste secara informal (membakar kabel, merendam papan sirkuit dengan asam) sangat berbahaya bagi pekerja dan lingkungan.

items.question: What kind of waste are broken chargers, circuit boards and TVs?
items.correct: B3 waste (e-waste)
wrong: Organic waste
Recyclable paper waste
Ordinary glass waste
items.explanation: The module includes broken electronics such as phones, chargers, circuit boards and TVs among the examples of household B3 waste.
items.quote: Elektronik rusak (e-waste): ponsel, charger, papan sirkuit, TV — Zat atau bahaya utama: Timbal, merkuri, kadmium, bahan penghambat api, baterai di dalamnya — Karakteristik terkait: Beracun

items.question: Which B3 characteristic do broken electronic devices have?
items.correct: Toxic
wrong: Infectious
Reactive
Explosive
items.explanation: In the household B3 examples, broken electronics are linked to the toxic characteristic because of the lead, mercury and cadmium inside them.
items.quote: Elektronik rusak (e-waste): ponsel, charger, papan sirkuit, TV — Zat atau bahaya utama: Timbal, merkuri, kadmium, bahan penghambat api, baterai di dalamnya — Karakteristik terkait: Beracun

items.question: If broken electronic devices go to the landfill with ordinary waste, how do their heavy metals pollute the groundwater?
items.correct: Through leachate, the liquid that seeps out of the waste pile
wrong: Through biogas from the waste pile
Through compost from the waste pile
Through worm castings
items.explanation: The module explains that B3 piling up in the landfill is carried by leachate, so heavy metals get into the soil and groundwater.
items.quote: B3 yang terbuang bersama sampah biasa menumpuk di TPA, lalu lindi (cairan rembesan) membawa logam berat ke tanah dan air tanah.

items.question: In the B3 management hierarchy, what is an example of 'reuse' for electronic devices?
items.correct: Repairing electronics so they last longer
wrong: Burning their cables to get the copper
Burying them in a special B3 landfill
Neutralising their acids and bases at home
items.explanation: The 'reuse' level of the B3 hierarchy means making things last longer, for example repairing electronics; burial is the last option.
items.quote: 2. Pakai ulang (reuse) — Tindakan: Perpanjang umur pakai — Contoh: Perbaiki elektronik, gunakan baterai isi ulang berulang kali, berbagi sisa cat yang masih layak.

items.question: Explain the recommended order of management for broken electronic devices, from prevention to burial.

rubricPoints.point: Avoid/reduce: choose products with no or little B3.
rubricPoints.quote: 1. Hindari/kurangi (reduce) — Tindakan: Pilih produk tanpa atau dengan sedikit B3 — Contoh: Lampu LED (tanpa merkuri), baterai isi ulang, pembersih ramah lingkungan, beli secukupnya.

rubricPoints.point: Reuse: make them last longer, for example by repairing electronics.
rubricPoints.quote: 2. Pakai ulang (reuse) — Tindakan: Perpanjang umur pakai — Contoh: Perbaiki elektronik, gunakan baterai isi ulang berulang kali, berbagi sisa cat yang masih layak.

rubricPoints.point: Recycle only through licensed facilities; informal recycling is very dangerous.
rubricPoints.quote: Daur ulang e-waste secara informal (membakar kabel, merendam papan sirkuit dengan asam) sangat berbahaya bagi pekerja dan lingkungan.

rubricPoints.point: Controlled burial in a special facility is the last option.
rubricPoints.quote: 5. Penimbunan terkontrol — Tindakan: Pilihan terakhir di fasilitas khusus — Contoh: Landfill khusus B3 dengan lapisan pelindung dan pemantauan.

objects.label: E_Waste

items.question: What kind of container should used batteries be collected in?
items.correct: A dry, closed container
wrong: A bucket of water
An open organic waste bin
A plastic bag together with food scraps
items.explanation: The module asks for used batteries to be collected in a dry, closed container, not burned and not taken apart.
items.quote: Kumpulkan dalam wadah kering tertutup; tutup kutub baterai litium dengan selotip; jangan dibakar atau dibongkar.

items.question: Why should the terminals of a used lithium battery be covered with tape before storing it?
items.correct: Because lithium batteries can catch fire if damaged or short-circuited
wrong: So the battery can go in an ordinary bin
So microorganisms break the battery down faster
So the battery is safe to burn
items.explanation: The module says lithium batteries can catch fire if damaged or short-circuited, so their terminals are taped and they are not burned.
items.quote: Logam berat (mis. kadmium pada Ni-Cd), elektrolit; baterai litium dapat terbakar jika rusak atau korslet.

items.question: Which B3 characteristics do used batteries have?
items.correct: Toxic, corrosive and flammable
wrong: Only infectious
Not dangerous once empty
Only explosive
items.explanation: In the household B3 examples, used batteries are linked to the toxic, corrosive and flammable characteristics.
items.quote: Baterai bekas (alkaline, Ni-Cd, litium) — Zat atau bahaya utama: Logam berat (mis. kadmium pada Ni-Cd), elektrolit; baterai litium dapat terbakar jika rusak atau korslet — Karakteristik terkait: Beracun, korosif, mudah menyala

items.question: Which materials can licensed facilities recover from used batteries?
items.correct: Metals such as nickel, cobalt, manganese and zinc, depending on the type
wrong: Glass and mercury, as in fluorescent tubes
Paper fibres to make new paper
Nothing; used batteries are only buried
items.explanation: The module says licensed facilities can recover metals such as nickel, cobalt, manganese and zinc from used batteries; people only need to collect and hand them in.
items.quote: Logam seperti nikel, kobalt, mangan, seng (tergantung jenis)

items.question: Explain how to store and hand in used batteries safely, with the reasons.

rubricPoints.point: Collect them in a dry, closed container and cover the terminals of lithium batteries with tape.
rubricPoints.quote: Kumpulkan dalam wadah kering tertutup; tutup kutub baterai litium dengan selotip; jangan dibakar atau dibongkar.

rubricPoints.point: Lithium batteries can catch fire if damaged or short-circuited.
rubricPoints.quote: Logam berat (mis. kadmium pada Ni-Cd), elektrolit; baterai litium dapat terbakar jika rusak atau korslet.

rubricPoints.point: Do not burn batteries.
rubricPoints.quote: Jangan membakar baterai, aerosol, atau sampah elektronik.

rubricPoints.point: Hand them in at a B3 or e-waste collection point, the environment office, or a manufacturer take-back programme.
rubricPoints.quote: Kumpulkan dalam wadah kering tertutup dan serahkan ke titik pengumpulan B3 atau e-waste, dinas lingkungan hidup, atau program take-back produsen.

objects.note: Aki kendaraan has its own row in 2.6/4.7 (hand to a workshop); not added as an object yet (not in the logs).

objects.label: E_Waste

items.question: Why are used fluorescent tubes, neon lamps and CFLs B3 waste?
items.correct: Because they contain mercury
wrong: Because they are made of plastic-coated paper
Because they can be broken down into compost
Because they contain sulphuric acid
items.explanation: The module says fluorescent tubes, neon lamps and CFLs contain mercury, so they are B3 waste; sulphuric acid is found in car batteries.
items.quote: Lampu bohlam pijar biasa terbuat dari kaca dan kawat logam, tetapi lampu TL, neon, dan lampu hemat energi (CFL) mengandung merkuri sehingga termasuk sampah B3 (Bab 2).

items.question: Which lamp is NOT B3 waste?
items.correct: An ordinary incandescent bulb
wrong: A fluorescent tube
A neon lamp
An energy-saving lamp (CFL)
items.explanation: The module separates ordinary incandescent bulbs (glass and metal wire) from fluorescent tubes, neon lamps and CFLs, which contain mercury.
items.quote: Lampu bohlam pijar biasa terbuat dari kaca dan kawat logam, tetapi lampu TL, neon, dan lampu hemat energi (CFL) mengandung merkuri sehingga termasuk sampah B3 (Bab 2).

items.question: How should a used fluorescent tube be stored before it is handed in?
items.correct: Intact, in its original packaging or a cardboard box
wrong: Broken first so it takes up less space
Mixed with ordinary glass waste
Burned so the mercury is used up
items.explanation: The module asks for fluorescent tubes, neon lamps and CFLs to be stored intact in their original packaging or a cardboard box and not thrown away with ordinary waste.
items.quote: Simpan utuh dalam kemasan asli atau kardus; jangan dibuang bersama sampah biasa.

items.question: A CFL breaks in a rented room. Which first step is safe?
items.correct: Getting people and pets away, opening the window and leaving the room for about 10-15 minutes
wrong: Sweeping up the pieces and throwing them in ordinary glass waste
Vacuuming the pieces
Burning the pieces so the mercury disappears
items.explanation: The module asks for the room to be aired first, then the pieces collected with card or sticky tape, without a broom or vacuum cleaner.
items.quote: Jauhkan anak-anak dan hewan peliharaan; buka jendela dan keluar dari ruangan sekitar 10 sampai 15 menit.

items.question: Explain why used fluorescent tubes or CFLs must be kept apart from ordinary glass waste, and how to handle them if they break.

rubricPoints.point: Fluorescent tubes, neon lamps and CFLs contain mercury, so they are B3.
rubricPoints.quote: Lampu bohlam pijar biasa terbuat dari kaca dan kawat logam, tetapi lampu TL, neon, dan lampu hemat energi (CFL) mengandung merkuri sehingga termasuk sampah B3 (Bab 2).

rubricPoints.point: Lamps are stored intact in their original packaging or a cardboard box.
rubricPoints.quote: Simpan utuh dalam kemasan asli atau kardus; jangan dibuang bersama sampah biasa.

rubricPoints.point: If one breaks, the room is aired and people leave for about 10-15 minutes.
rubricPoints.quote: Jauhkan anak-anak dan hewan peliharaan; buka jendela dan keluar dari ruangan sekitar 10 sampai 15 menit.

rubricPoints.point: The pieces go into a closed container and are treated as B3 waste.
rubricPoints.quote: 3. Masukkan semua pecahan ke wadah tertutup (misalnya toples kaca bertutup) dan perlakukan sebagai sampah B3.

objects.note: "lampu" alone also maps here; question 2 covers the incandescent exception. LED is mentioned only in 2.9 (mercury-free).

items.question: What type of plastic are plastic drink bottles usually made of?
items.correct: PET
wrong: HDPE
PVC
Styrofoam (polystyrene foam)
items.explanation: The module names plastic drink bottles as PET; HDPE and PVC are used for other products.
items.quote: Botol plastik minuman (PET), kantong kresek, sedotan dan peralatan makan sekali pakai.

items.question: When PET bottles are sorted for recycling, which resin identification code is used?
items.correct: Code 1
wrong: Code 2
Code 3
Code 4
items.explanation: The first stage of plastic recycling is sorting by resin identification code, with 1 for PET and 2 for HDPE.
items.quote: 1. Pengumpulan dan pemilahan berdasarkan kode jenis resin (1 = PET, 2 = HDPE, dan seterusnya).

items.question: PET bottle flakes are put in a water tank. What happens?
items.correct: They sink, because their density is higher than water's
wrong: They float, because their density is lower than water's
They dissolve in the water
They float, just like HDPE
items.explanation: The worked example in the module shows PET (1.38) sinks and HDPE (0.95) floats compared with water (1.00).
items.quote: Jawab: HDPE (0,95 < 1,00) mengapung dan diambil dari permukaan; PET (1,38 > 1,00) tenggelam dan diambil dari dasar.

items.question: At about what temperature are plastic bottle flakes melted when recycled?
items.correct: About 200-300°C
wrong: About 660°C
About 1538°C
About 50-70°C
items.explanation: The module says plastic is melted at about 200-300°C; 660°C and 1538°C are the melting temperatures of aluminium and iron.
items.quote: 4. Peleburan pada suhu tinggi (sekitar 200-300°C).

items.question: Explain the stages of recycling a plastic bottle until it becomes material for new products.

rubricPoints.point: Bottles are sorted by resin identification code (PET = 1).
rubricPoints.quote: 1. Pengumpulan dan pemilahan berdasarkan kode jenis resin (1 = PET, 2 = HDPE, dan seterusnya).

rubricPoints.point: The bottles are cleaned and then shredded into flakes.
rubricPoints.quote: 3. Pencacahan (shredding) menjadi serpihan (flakes).

rubricPoints.point: The flakes are melted at a high temperature.
rubricPoints.quote: 4. Peleburan pada suhu tinggi (sekitar 200-300°C).

rubricPoints.point: The melt is formed into recycled plastic pellets.
rubricPoints.quote: 5. Pembentukan pelet plastik daur ulang.

objects.label: Plastic

items.question: Which waste group does a disposable plastic cup belong to?
items.correct: Non-organic, because it is made of synthetic material that is very hard to break down
wrong: Organic, because microorganisms can break it down
B3, because it contains mercury
Organic, because it comes from plants
items.explanation: The module classes plastic as non-organic waste made of synthetic material that is very hard for microorganisms to break down.
items.quote: Sampah non-organik berasal dari bahan sintetis atau bahan anorganis yang tidak dapat atau sangat sulit diuraikan mikroorganisme.

items.question: According to the 3R priority order, which action comes first for disposable plastic cups?
items.correct: Using fewer of them in the first place (reduce)
wrong: Recycling them, because recycle comes first
Using them again, because reuse comes before reduce
Burying them in the landfill
items.explanation: The module says reduce comes before reuse, and reuse comes before recycle.
items.quote: Urutan menunjukkan prioritas: Reduce lebih utama daripada Reuse, dan Reuse lebih utama daripada Recycle.

items.question: Which personal action is recommended for disposable plastic cups?
items.correct: Avoiding single-use plastic and choosing environmentally friendly products
wrong: Throwing plastic cups away with organic waste
Burning plastic cups in the yard
Burying plastic cups in the soil so they break down
items.explanation: According to the module, a person's role includes avoiding single-use plastic and choosing environmentally friendly products.
items.quote: Menghindari plastik sekali pakai dan memilih produk ramah lingkungan.

items.question: Explain why we should use fewer disposable plastic cups, based on the properties of plastic waste and the 3R principle.

rubricPoints.point: Plastic comes from synthetic materials that are very hard for microorganisms to break down.
rubricPoints.quote: Sampah non-organik berasal dari bahan sintetis atau bahan anorganis yang tidak dapat atau sangat sulit diuraikan mikroorganisme.

rubricPoints.point: In the 3Rs, reduce comes first.
rubricPoints.quote: Urutan menunjukkan prioritas: Reduce lebih utama daripada Reuse, dan Reuse lebih utama daripada Recycle.

rubricPoints.point: People are encouraged to avoid single-use plastic.
rubricPoints.quote: Menghindari plastik sekali pakai dan memilih produk ramah lingkungan.

objects.note: Thin: the module names "gelas sekali pakai" only in the 4.2 resin table (not converted), so 3 MC.

items.question: Which waste group does a used glass jar belong to?
items.correct: Non-organic (inorganic)
wrong: Organic, because it breaks down easily
B3, because it contains mercury
Residual waste that cannot be recycled
items.explanation: The module gives glass as an example of non-organic waste that is synthetic or mineral and does not break down easily.
items.quote: Non-organik (anorganik) — Ciri utama: Sintetis atau mineral, tidak mudah terurai — Contoh: Botol plastik, kaleng, kaca

items.question: Before melting, how are used glass jars sorted?
items.correct: By their colour
wrong: By their resin identification code
By their magnetic properties
By their moisture content
items.explanation: The module says glass is sorted by colour, washed, crushed (cullet), melted and formed again.
items.quote: Kaca: dipilah menurut warna, dicuci, dihancurkan (cullet), dilebur, dan dibentuk ulang.

items.question: What should be done with a glass jar that is still intact?
items.correct: Use it again (reuse)
wrong: Break it and hand it in as B3
Compost it
Burn it with other waste
items.explanation: The module says intact glass bottles or containers are better reused.
items.quote: Kaca dapat didaur ulang berkali-kali tanpa kehilangan mutu; botol utuh lebih baik dipakai ulang (reuse).

items.question: What advantage does glass have over paper when it comes to recycling?
items.correct: Glass can be recycled many times without losing quality
wrong: Glass can only be recycled about 5-7 times
Glass must be separated with a magnet before melting
Glass can be composted after it is crushed
items.explanation: The module says glass does not lose quality when recycled, while paper only lasts about 5-7 times because its fibres get shorter.
items.quote: Kaca dapat didaur ulang berkali-kali tanpa kehilangan mutu; botol utuh lebih baik dipakai ulang (reuse).

items.question: Explain how used glass jars are recycled and why intact ones are better reused.

rubricPoints.point: Glass is sorted by colour, washed, crushed (cullet), melted and formed again.
rubricPoints.quote: Kaca: dipilah menurut warna, dicuci, dihancurkan (cullet), dilebur, dan dibentuk ulang.

rubricPoints.point: Glass can be recycled many times without losing quality.
rubricPoints.quote: Kaca dapat didaur ulang berkali-kali tanpa kehilangan mutu; botol utuh lebih baik dipakai ulang (reuse).

rubricPoints.point: In the 3Rs, reuse comes before recycle.
rubricPoints.quote: Urutan menunjukkan prioritas: Reduce lebih utama daripada Reuse, dan Reuse lebih utama daripada Recycle.

items.question: Roughly how much energy does recycling an aluminium can need compared with making aluminium from bauxite ore?
items.correct: About 5%
wrong: About 50%
About 95%
About 100%
items.explanation: The module says recycling aluminium needs only about 5% of the energy; 95% is the saving.
items.quote: Daur ulang logam, khususnya aluminium, sangat hemat energi: mendaur ulang aluminium hanya memerlukan sekitar 5% energi dibanding membuatnya dari bijih bauksit (Tchobanoglous dkk., 1993).

items.question: What is a simple way to tell an aluminium can from a steel can?
items.correct: Hold a magnet near it: the aluminium can does not stick
wrong: Hold a magnet near it: the aluminium can sticks
Read the resin identification code on the can
Sort the cans by colour, like glass
items.explanation: The module explains that iron and steel are attracted to magnets, while aluminium is not.
items.quote: Logam feromagnetik (besi, baja) tertarik magnet, sedangkan aluminium, tembaga, kaca, dan plastik tidak.

items.question: At about what temperature are aluminium cans melted in a furnace?
items.correct: About 660°C
wrong: About 1538°C
About 200-300°C
About 50-70°C
items.explanation: The module says aluminium is melted at about 660°C and iron at about 1538°C.
items.quote: 3. Peleburan di tanur: aluminium sekitar 660°C, besi sekitar 1538°C.

items.question: In theory, melting 1 kg of aluminium from 25°C needs about 0.97 MJ. Why does a real furnace need more energy?
items.correct: Because heat is lost; that calculation is only the minimum energy
wrong: Because aluminium has to be heated to about 1538°C
Because the energy for bauxite electrolysis is included
Because the latent heat of melting aluminium was left out
items.explanation: The module stresses that 0.97 MJ is the theoretical limit and real furnaces need more because of heat losses.
items.quote: Ini hanya energi minimum untuk meleburkan; tanur nyata memerlukan lebih banyak karena rugi panas.

items.question: Explain why recycling aluminium cans is strongly recommended and how aluminium cans are separated from steel cans.

rubricPoints.point: Recycling aluminium needs only about 5% of the energy of producing it from bauxite.
rubricPoints.quote: Daur ulang logam, khususnya aluminium, sangat hemat energi: mendaur ulang aluminium hanya memerlukan sekitar 5% energi dibanding membuatnya dari bijih bauksit (Tchobanoglous dkk., 1993).

rubricPoints.point: Melting needs far less energy than producing it from bauxite by electrolysis.
rubricPoints.quote: Namun nilai ini jauh lebih kecil daripada energi untuk memproduksi aluminium dari bauksit lewat elektrolisis, yang menjadi dasar klaim bahwa daur ulang aluminium hemat sekitar 95% energi.

rubricPoints.point: Metals are sorted by type; a magnet separates iron-based metals.
rubricPoints.quote: 1. Pengumpulan dan pemilahan menurut jenis logam (magnet dapat memisahkan logam besi).

rubricPoints.point: Aluminium is not attracted to magnets, while steel is.
rubricPoints.quote: Logam feromagnetik (besi, baja) tertarik magnet, sedangkan aluminium, tembaga, kaca, dan plastik tidak.

items.question: Why can plain cardboard without a plastic or aluminium foil layer break down naturally?
items.correct: Because it comes from plant fibres that microorganisms can break down
wrong: Because it contains mercury, which speeds up decomposition
Because it is made of synthetic material that microorganisms break down easily
Because the aluminium foil layer helps microorganisms break it down

items.question: In everyday sorting, why is used cardboard often put with recyclable inorganic waste?
items.correct: Because it is worth more when recycled into new paper
wrong: Because cardboard cannot break down
Because cardboard contains hazardous materials
Because cardboard is attracted to magnets
items.explanation: Cardboard comes from plant fibres and can break down, but it is often put with recyclable inorganic waste because it is worth more recycled.
items.quote: Kertas dan karton berasal dari serat tumbuhan sehingga dapat terurai, tetapi di sistem pemilahan sehari-hari sering ditaruh pada kelompok anorganik daur ulang karena lebih bernilai bila didaur ulang menjadi kertas baru (lihat Bab 4).

items.question: What about cardboard that is plastic-coated or greasy?
items.correct: It is not suitable for composting
wrong: It breaks down faster than plain cardboard
It is B3 waste
It must be burned in the yard
items.explanation: The module says plastic-coated, greasy or laminated paper is not suitable for composting.
items.quote: Kertas berlapis plastik, berminyak, atau berlaminasi (misalnya kemasan karton minuman, lihat 4.6) tidak cocok dikomposkan.

items.question: Why can used cardboard not be recycled endlessly?
items.correct: Its cellulose fibres get shorter every time it is recycled
wrong: Its ink cannot be removed
Cardboard must be melted at high temperatures like metal
Cardboard is B3, so it may not be recycled
items.explanation: The module explains that paper's cellulose fibres get shorter with each recycling, so it only lasts about 5-7 times.
items.quote: Serat selulosa kertas memendek setiap kali didaur ulang, sehingga kertas dapat didaur ulang sekitar 5-7 kali (Arief, 2016).

rubricPoints.quote: Serat selulosa kertas memendek setiap kali didaur ulang, sehingga kertas dapat didaur ulang sekitar 5-7 kali (Arief, 2016).

items.question: Used paper can break down because of what it is made from. What is that?

Mineral materials
Plastic and aluminium layers

items.question: When recycling used paper, what happens in the de-inking stage?
items.correct: The ink is removed from the paper
wrong: The paper is melted into pellets
The paper is separated with a magnet
The paper is coated with plastic
items.explanation: In the paper recycling stages, de-inking is ink removal; pellets and magnets are used for plastic and metal.
items.quote: 3. Penghilangan tinta (de-inking).

items.question: About how many times can used paper be recycled?
items.correct: About 5-7 times
wrong: About 1 time
About 20 times
About 100 times
items.explanation: The module says cellulose fibres get shorter with each recycling, so paper can be recycled about 5-7 times.
items.quote: Serat selulosa kertas memendek setiap kali didaur ulang, sehingga kertas dapat didaur ulang sekitar 5-7 kali (Arief, 2016).

items.question: How should greasy paper from a fried-food wrapper be processed?
items.correct: It is not suitable for composting, unlike plain paper
wrong: It is good for vermicompost because the oil helps the worms
It is B3 waste
It breaks down faster because of its oil
items.explanation: The module says greasy paper is not suitable for composting, and vermicompost avoids oily food.
items.quote: Kertas berlapis plastik, berminyak, atau berlaminasi (misalnya kemasan karton minuman, lihat 4.6) tidak cocok dikomposkan.

items.question: Which waste group does a banana peel belong to?
items.correct: Organic, because it comes from a living thing and can break down
wrong: Non-organic, because it is hard to break down
B3, because it is toxic
Residual waste that cannot be processed
items.explanation: The module puts fruit peels such as banana peels in organic waste: waste from living things that can break down.
items.quote: Kulit buah: kulit pisang, kulit jeruk, kulit melon.

items.question: Banana peels are processed by vermicomposting. What is the end product?
items.correct: Nutrient-rich worm castings
wrong: Biogas containing methane
Recycled plastic pellets
Leachate for watering plants
items.explanation: Vermicomposting uses earthworms, and its end product is nutrient-rich worm castings.
items.quote: Hasil akhirnya kascing (bekas cacing) yang kaya unsur hara dan lebih cepat diserap tanaman (Damanhuri dan Padmi, 2010, hal. 92-97).

items.question: Which material should NOT go into a vermicompost bin together with banana peels?
items.correct: Meat and oily food
wrong: Vegetable scraps
Leaves
Paper without oil
items.explanation: The module says vegetable scraps, fruit peels, leaves and paper without oil are suitable, while meat and oily food are avoided.
items.quote: Hindari: daging, produk susu, makanan berminyak, dan bahan berbau menyengat.

items.question: If banana peels and food scraps are processed without oxygen in a closed digester, what is produced?
items.correct: Biogas from anaerobic fermentation by methanogenic bacteria
wrong: Worm castings from earthworms
Recycled plastic pellets
Mercury from rotting
items.explanation: The module explains that biogas is produced by anaerobic fermentation of organic matter by methanogenic bacteria.
items.quote: Biogas dihasilkan dari fermentasi anaerobik bahan organik oleh bakteri metanogen.

items.question: Explain why banana peels and food scraps should be turned into worm castings or biogas instead of going to the landfill.

rubricPoints.point: Organic waste rotting without oxygen in the landfill produces methane, a greenhouse gas.
rubricPoints.quote: Sampah organik yang membusuk tanpa oksigen di TPA menghasilkan metana, gas rumah kaca dengan potensi pemanasan sekitar 25-28 kali CO2.

rubricPoints.point: Vermicomposting produces nutrient-rich worm castings.
rubricPoints.quote: Hasil akhirnya kascing (bekas cacing) yang kaya unsur hara dan lebih cepat diserap tanaman (Damanhuri dan Padmi, 2010, hal. 92-97).

rubricPoints.point: Biogas is produced by anaerobic fermentation of organic matter.
rubricPoints.quote: Biogas dihasilkan dari fermentasi anaerobik bahan organik oleh bakteri metanogen.

items.question: What kind of packaging is a used milk carton?
items.correct: Multilayer packaging
wrong: Metal packaging without layers
Plain paper packaging without layers
Glass packaging
items.explanation: The module calls drink cartons such as milk cartons multilayer packaging.
items.quote: Kemasan karton minuman, misalnya kotak susu atau jus (sering dikenal dengan merek Tetra Pak), adalah kemasan berlapis (multilayer).

items.question: Why is a used milk carton not composted, even though it is mostly paper?
items.correct: Its plastic and aluminium layers mean the milk carton cannot be composted
wrong: Its paper contains mercury
Milk cartons are B3 waste
Its paper cannot be recycled at all
items.explanation: Milk cartons have plastic and aluminium layers, so they are recyclable non-organic waste, not compost.
items.quote: Kemasan karton minuman bekas termasuk sampah non-organik yang dapat didaur ulang meskipun sebagian besar bahannya kertas, karena berlapis plastik dan aluminium sehingga tidak dapat dikomposkan.

items.question: What do the plastic and aluminium layers in a milk carton do?
items.correct: They keep the drink fresh and stop leaks
wrong: They make the milk carton easy to compost
They make the milk carton stick to a magnet when sorted
They make the milk carton B3 waste
items.explanation: The module says the plastic and aluminium layers keep the drink fresh and stop leaks.
items.quote: Lapisan plastik dan aluminium menjaga isi minuman tetap awet dan tidak bocor.

items.question: In milk carton recycling, what happens in the pulper?
items.correct: The carton is mixed with water so the paper fibres come away from the plastic and aluminium layers
wrong: The carton is melted at about 660°C to take out its aluminium
The carton is separated with a magnet
The carton is composted so its plastic breaks down
items.explanation: According to the recycling stages the module quotes from Tetra Pak Indonesia, pulping uses water to free the fibres from the plastic and aluminium.
items.quote: 2. Pulping: karton dicampur dengan air di mesin pulper sehingga serat kertas terlepas dari lapisan plastik dan aluminium.

items.question: Describe how used milk cartons are recycled in a facility that separates the fibres from the PolyAl layer.

rubricPoints.point: Pulping frees the paper fibres from the plastic and aluminium layers.
rubricPoints.quote: 2. Pulping: karton dicampur dengan air di mesin pulper sehingga serat kertas terlepas dari lapisan plastik dan aluminium.

rubricPoints.point: The fibres are cleaned, dried and then made into new paper sheets.
rubricPoints.quote: 3. Daur ulang serat: serat dibersihkan, diperas, dikeringkan, lalu dibuat menjadi lembaran kertas baru.

rubricPoints.point: The leftover plastic and aluminium (PolyAl) is shredded and processed into granules.
rubricPoints.quote: 4. Daur ulang PolyAl: plastik dan aluminium yang tersisa dicacah dan diolah menjadi granul.

rubricPoints.point: Its products include paper and corrugated roofing sheets.
rubricPoints.quote: 5. Produk: serat kertas menjadi produk kertas; PolyAl menjadi antara lain lembar atap gelombang.
